_schema: Every numeric entry is {v, unit, conf, src, note?}. Units: mm and deg, in the machine frame of the keyboard unit (Blender, Z up): origin at the centre of the case footprint on its bottom face, +X left to right as the operator sees the keyboard, +Y toward the back, +Z up. conf: doc = stated in a document or museum record; model = read off RetroStack's reconstruction (case STL or KiCad board, research/tools/), which its author compared with an original; photo = scaled from a photo; est = estimate, to be checked; design = our own choice where sources are silent. Source keys are in research/bibliography.md. Positions read off the case STL convert as X = x_stl + 215, Y = -(z_stl + 102.5), Z = y_stl. keyboard.json and board.json are generated from this file and the KiCad part lists by tools/kicad_to_params.py; never edit them by hand.
reference_machine: TRS-80 Model I keyboard unit, Level II 16 KB, 1979: main board revision G, ALPS keyboard with the 12-key numeric keypad (design/decisions/0001-which-machine.md)

take_apart.src: Open: the 1978 Technical Manual has no disassembly section; a service-manual excerpt of unclear model (manualshive) and trs-80.com's modification notes suggest the order below. Confirm from the Model I service manual or photos

order.path: each plug back 60 mm out of its socket
up 140 mm, after four screws from the underside
up 90 mm; its flat cable to J100 limits the travel
up 45 mm so the DIN sockets clear the rear panel, then 250 mm forward, where it turns over to show its parts

enclosure.note: Two shells. The outer, silver shell is an open tray (a 'dustpan'): a floor, two side walls and a rear wall, with no top and no front. The inner, dark shell holds the tube and sits in it; its top and front are the monitor's top and front. A groove runs between them along both sides (on the top and on the front) and across the lower front, above the floor. Replaces the earlier tapered back (open item O9), which had no source.

cable_jacks.src: the TRS-80 cassette cable's three plugs: EAR (the recorder's output, read by the computer), AUX (the computer's output, recorded), REM (the motor, switched by the computer's relay)

sides.note: seen from either side the body is three horizontal parts (a side-by-side comparison with the photos, 2026-11-12; review: the three parts differ only a little in height): a smooth upper part carrying the rounded top edge, a ribbed middle part standing a little proud of it, and a smooth lower part set in. The ribs stop short of a plain block at the front end and just short of the rear

ribs_y.note: a plain block of about 19 mm at the front end, 5 mm at the rear (ctr80a_05)

sides.src: ctr80a_05 re-measured by where the ribs' texture is (rows 212-247 of 168-271: upper 43 %, ribs 34 %, lower 23 %); review, 2026-11-12: a shorter ribbed part, a taller lower part

jack_panel.src: ctr80a_06, the left side straight on (375 px over 240 mm: 0.64 mm/px)

front_recess.src: review, 2026-11-12: the black base under the silver strip is indented about 2-3 mm across its middle third

power_supply.src: two reference photos of the whole system, 2026-11-12 (a colour photo with the CTR-80A and its box; a Radio Shack black-and-white publicity photo; web images, not in the repo); Computer History Museum catalogue 102728699 / 102786948 (a 2-wire mains cord and a separate cord with a 5-pin DIN plug); about 14 V AC out (Radio Shack technical reference)
power_supply.note: A small black transformer box, slightly tapered: the top a little smaller than the base, the vertical corners rounded, a plain raised panel on top, a groove round the sides near the bottom. Its DIN cord leaves the front, low down; the mains cord the back

size.src: two reference photos of the whole system, 2026-11-12 (a colour photo with the CTR-80A and its box; a Radio Shack black-and-white publicity photo; web images, not in the repo): about 70 px tall beside the recorder's 46 mm front (about 48 px) in the colour photo; est within about 10 %

top.src: two reference photos of the whole system, 2026-11-12 (a colour photo with the CTR-80A and its box; a Radio Shack black-and-white publicity photo; web images, not in the repo): the top a little smaller than the base

top_panel.src: two reference photos of the whole system, 2026-11-12 (a colour photo with the CTR-80A and its box; a Radio Shack black-and-white publicity photo; web images, not in the repo); review, 2026-11-12: a plain raised surface; the lines across it in the photos are a sticker's print, not modelled
